newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF rate cut likely on Thursday - economists.
newsitem.headline: BoF rate cut likely on Thursday - economists.

text.p: The Bank of France will probably cut its key intervention rate on Thursday if the government's 1997 budget is well received by the markets and the franc holds near its current levels, most economists said.
Some said the bank might limit itself to lowering call money as a signal to markets of more rate cuts ahead while waiting for potentially negative reaction to the budget to pass.

"Given the state of the franc, if the Bank of France wants to reinforce the idea that the budget is credible, it could cut the intervention rate by 10 basis points," said Deutsche Bank economist Patrick Mange in Paris.
"If they don't do it Thursday, I would not be surprised, but it will be a case of the bank taking a step back to be able to make a bigger leap," Mange said.
The Bank of France's monetary policy council meets on Thursday and analysts said any intervention rate cut would probably be announced at the money market tender at 1115 GMT.
Most analysts said the intervention rate could be cut by 10 basis points. No analysts expected the five-to-10 day emergency lending rate to be lowered this week.
The intervention rate is currently at 3.35 percent and was last cut from 3.55 percent on August 22. The Bank's five-to-10 day rate is 4.75 percent and was last cut, by 15 basis points, on August 1.

Economists said the Bank of France had many reasons to cut rates. Inflation is low, the economy is stagnant, French M3 money supply fell in June and July, and the spread between the Bundesbank's repo rate and the intervention rate is 35 basis points, wider than before the August 22 round of rate cuts.

The only sticking point is some lingering uncertainty over how financial markets will receive France's 1997 budget, which marries tax cuts with austerity and aims to bring public deficits down to three percent of gross domestic product.
But most market participants appear to have accepted the government's word that it will achieve the target.
French government bond (OATs) prices have risen during the past week, interest rate futures were also on the rise and the franc was stronger at 3.4006 per mark.

"The mood seems to have changed and if the budget gets a good reception, they could go ahead," said Sonja Gibbs, economist at Nomura International in London. "As long as the franc holds up," she said.

Analysts who said an intervention rate cut was not likely said the Bank would probably lower call money, a semi-official interest rate, to let the market know more intervention rate cuts were on the way.

"I think the Bank of France will lower call money on Thursday," said Morgan Stanley economist Eric Chaney. "I don't exclude a small cut in the intervention rate but traditionally, the Bank signals a cut by lowering call money."
Call money has been unchanged at 3-7/16 9/16 percent since August 23.
